lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: After a long drought, the LORD told Elijah to show himself to Ahab. The time had come to announce that rain would return.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ahab's official Obadiah had secretly protected a hundred prophets of the LORD from Jezebel. But now Elijah stood openly before the king.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Gather all Israel on Mount Carmel. Bring the prophets of Baal. Let the people see who truly answers prayer.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: How long will you keep wavering? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is God, follow him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The prophets of Baal cried out from morning until noon. They called, shouted, and performed their rituals—but there was no answer.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Cry louder! Perhaps your god is busy, travelling, or asleep and needs to be awakened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Elijah repaired the LORD's broken-down altar. He used twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel, and had the sacrifice and wood soaked with water.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, show today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant. Answer me, LORD!

choices.label: Pray with confidence
choices.note: Elijah's prayer is not a performance. He asks God to turn the people's hearts back to him.

choices.label: Remember who must receive the glory
choices.note: The sign is meant to reveal the LORD—not to make Elijah famous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the fire of the LORD fell. It consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the soil, and even the water in the trench.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The people fell facedown and cried out: The LORD—he is God! The LORD—he is God!

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Go back and look toward the sea. The drought is ending.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small cloud appeared. The sky grew dark, the wind rose, and soon the land was filled with rain.
